title: bug: isEpicFinal follows the highest board order, so any dragged or newly created row becomes "epic-final"
description:
Rule today, mirrored in two places: packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/policy.ts:202 isEpicFinalTask() and tools/getContext.ts:348. Epic-final means the highest `order` among the epic's non-ARCHIVED tasks, ties counting.

But `order` is a per-column sort position. A board drag or set_task_status move puts a row at the end of its new column (e.g. 229.5/230.5 in PLANNING), and create_task appends new rows at max+1. So the flag drifts to whichever row was last moved or created.

Measured 2026-10-25, five of six CQ epics flag the wrong row:
- CQ-F flags F04b (230.5); the real final is F12 "Contract integration and hardening" (120).
- CQ-R flags R01 (226.5); the real final is R13 (130).
- CQ-V flags V01 (227.5); the real final is V12 (120).
- CQ-C flags C03 (224.5); the real final is C11 (110).
- CQ-I flags I03 (228.5); the real final is I06 (60).
- Only CQ-M (M06) is right, by coincidence.

Impact: get_context hands architects isEpicFinal, and moe-planning / architect.md put full regression, integration coverage, the docs sweep and the whole-epic adversarial pass on the epic's final task only. Mid-epic rows get over-gated and the real hardening rows get under-gated. Projects with settings.qualityGate also run the wrapper's landing gate on the wrong row (requiredCheckCommand); this project has no qualityGate, so no landing is affected today.

A fix must name the final task independently of board position. Two candidate rules: an explicit, persisted designation set when the epic is broken down and editable later; or the epic task whose dependsOn closure covers every other non-ARCHIVED task in the epic. Keep policy.ts and getContext.ts on one shared helper, which the existing pin test should enforce.
definitionOfDone: Dragging a row to the end of any column, moving it via set_task_status, or creating a new row in an epic does not change which task get_context reports as isEpicFinal; covered by daemon tests.

Each CQ epic's "integration and hardening" row (F12, R13, V12, C11, I06, M06) reports isEpicFinal true, and their mid-epic siblings report false, under the new rule. Existing epics without a designation keep a deterministic, documented fallback.

isEpicFinalTask (delivery/policy.ts) and get_context's isEpicFinal use one shared implementation, the existing pin test still passes, and docs/MCP_SERVER.md and the moe-planning skill describe the rule.
Fresh `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits 0 with output supplied to complete_task.

implementationPlan.description:
Persist an explicit epic-final designation and give agents one validated way to set it. TDD: write the updateEpic.test.ts cases first and watch them fail.

1. schema.ts `interface Epic` (~L384): add `finalTaskId?: string` with a doc comment. It is the epic's designated final (integration-and-hardening) task, set or cleared with moe.update_epic. It counts only while it names an existing, non-ARCHIVED task of this epic; otherwise isEpicFinalTask (delivery/policy.ts) falls back to the highest `order`. The field is optional, so existing .moe/epics/*.json files without the key load unchanged (persistence.loadEntities keeps every field), and the JetBrains Gson `Epic` model and the VS Code `Epic` type ignore it.

2. validators.ts `validateEpicUpdates` (~L513): add 'finalTaskId' to the rejectUnknownFields allow-list. Shape-check it with `validateStringValue(input.finalTaskId, 'finalTaskId', { maxLength: 200, allowEmpty: true, trim: true })`, which rejects a non-string, a NUL or newline, and an over-long id. An empty or all-space value clears the designation: set `sanitized.finalTaskId = undefined`, so the `{ ...epic, ...sanitized }` merge in StateManager.updateEpic drops the key from the written JSON. In `epicUpdatedActivityPayload` (~L571), when `updates` has its own 'finalTaskId', record `payload.finalTaskId = epic.finalTaskId ?? null`.

3. updateEpic.ts: add to inputSchema.properties `finalTaskId: { type: 'string', description: "Designate the epic's final (integration-and-hardening) task by id. get_context isEpicFinal and the epicFinal quality-gate scope follow it whatever the board order. An empty string clears it, and the epic falls back to the highest order." }`. Add 'finalTaskId' to allowedFields and to the params/updates types, and pass it through to `updates` untouched (validators trims it).

The error handling lives in the tool and runs before any write. Run the cross-entity check only when finalTaskId is a string whose trimmed value is non-empty AND state.getEpic(epicId) exists:
- a missing epic keeps today's `Epic not found` error from state.updateEpic;
- a non-string falls through to the validators' `must be a string`.
The check throws invalidInput('finalTaskId', ...), whose message reads `Invalid finalTaskId: ...`, in three cases:
- state.getTask(id) is null: `names no task: <id>`;
- task.epicId !== epicId: `task <id> belongs to epic <task.epicId>, not <epicId>`;
- task.status === 'ARCHIVED': `task <id> is ARCHIVED and can never be epic-final`.
The board's UPDATE_EPIC path (WebSocketServer) reaches validateEpicUpdates only, so it gets the shape check alone. That is safe because step 2's read-time validity check ignores a dangling id.

4. updateEpic.test.ts: add these cases beside the existing ones.
(a) Designating a task of the epic persists `finalTaskId` (h.state.getEpic) and survives a reload: `await h.state.load()` again, or read .moe/epics/epic-1.json back from disk.
(b) '' and '   ' each clear a set designation (getEpic(...).finalTaskId is undefined).
(c) An unknown id, a task in another epic, and an ARCHIVED task each reject with a message containing 'finalTaskId'. Send each one together with a `title`, and assert the stored epic keeps its original title and designation, so nothing partial is written.
(d) `finalTaskId: 42` rejects with `must be a string`.
(e) A whitespace-padded valid id is stored trimmed.
Keep 'rejects unknown epic update fields before applying allowed fields' passing unchanged.

Focused check for this step: `cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/tools/updateEpic.test.ts`.

Make isEpicFinalTask the single epic-final rule and point get_context at it. TDD: write the tests first and watch them fail.

1. delivery/policy.ts `isEpicFinalTask(state, task)` (~L202):
- A task with no epicId is final (unchanged).
- Designation: read `state.getEpic(task.epicId)?.finalTaskId`. It counts only when it is a non-empty string, `state.getTask(id)` exists, that task's epicId equals task.epicId, and its status is not ARCHIVED. Then return `task.id === id`. Check `typeof === 'string'`, so a hand-edited null or number in an epic file is ignored rather than crashing.
- Otherwise keep today's fallback code verbatim: the highest finite `order` among the epic's non-ARCHIVED tasks, ties counting, with a non-finite order read as 0. Undesignated epics therefore behave exactly as before. These existing tests must pass unchanged: 'isEpicFinal: highest order wins, ties count, ARCHIVED siblings are ignored' (getContext.test.ts) and the pin test 'decides epic-final exactly as get_context does, including ties, ARCHIVED tasks and other epics' (qaApprove.test.ts).
- Rewrite the doc comment. State the rule, and say why `order` alone is wrong: it is a per-column sort position that board drags, set_task_status moves and create_task's max+1 rewrite. Say that requiredCheckCommand, qa_approve's requiredCheckAtDone snapshot and get_context all call this one function.

2. tools/getContext.ts:
- Replace the inline block (~L419-432, comment 'Epic-final = highest `order` among the epic's non-ARCHIVED tasks') with `const isEpicFinal = task ? isEpicFinalTask(state, task) : undefined;`.
- Import isEpicFinalTask from '../delivery/policy.js'. getContext already reaches that module through ../state/dependencyUnblock.js, so this adds no new import cycle.
- Rewrite the comment to name the shared rule, and drop the claim that the wrapper computes the same rule. The list_tasks+python fallback in scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1} runs only against daemons that do not serve isEpicFinal, and those use the highest-order rule, so leave the scripts untouched.
- In the `epic` projection (~L484), add `...(epic.finalTaskId ? { finalTaskId: epic.finalTaskId } : {})` so a planner can see the designated task.

3. getContext.test.ts: read isEpicFinal through `getContextTool(h.state).handler({ taskId }, h.state)`, and designate through `updateEpicTool(h.state).handler({ epicId, finalTaskId }, h.state)`.
(a) DoD 1: 'a designated final task stays epic-final across board drags, set_task_status moves and new rows'. Set up epic-1 with task-a (BACKLOG, order 1), task-b (WORKING, order 2) and task-final (BACKLOG, order 3), and designate task-final. After EACH of these moves, assert task-final reads true and the moved or new row reads false:
   (1) A JetBrains board drag. Its UPDATE_TASK {status, order} lands as `h.state.updateTask('task-b', { order: 3.5 })`.
   (2) setTaskStatusTool BACKLOG->PLANNING on task-a, then the board's end-of-column order: `h.state.updateTask('task-a', { order: 4.5 })`.
   (3) The REORDER_TASK path: `h.state.reorderTask('task-b', 'task-a', null)`, which lands at 5.5.
   (4) createTaskTool({ epicId: 'epic-1', title: 'late bug row' }), which gets the epic's max order + 1.
(b) Control: the same drag in an undesignated epic makes the dragged row true and task-final false. This proves the assertions catch the old behaviour and documents the fallback's drift.
(c) Deterministic fallback. Write a designation straight into the fixture (`h.createEpic({ finalTaskId: ... })`) that names a missing task, a task of another epic, or an ARCHIVED task. Each is ignored and the epic answers with the highest-order rule, ties counting. Assert the exact true/false of every row. Clearing with update_epic '' does the same.
(d) The `epic` projection carries finalTaskId when a task is designated and omits it otherwise.

Describe the rule where DoD 3 asks for it.

It is true for the epic's designated final task (`epic.finalTaskId`, set with moe.update_epic), so board drags, set_task_status moves and new rows never move it. planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Measured on the 2026-10-26 board before choosing a rule.
(1) A dependsOn-closure rule (the task whose closure covers every other non-ARCHIVED epic task) finds C11, I06 and V12, but no task in CQ-F, CQ-M or CQ-R, because later bug rows sit outside the hardening task's closure. Any new row without dependencies breaks it, so it also fails DoD 1.
(2) A max-closure rule picks bc8410af over F12 in CQ-F, because bc8410af depends on F12. In an epic with no edges, every row ties.
(3) A title heuristic ('integration and hardening', or createTask's META_TITLE_RE) depends on brittle free text.
(4) A per-task flag allows several finals per epic and travels with a task that moves to another epic.
Chosen: Epic.finalTaskId. It is single-valued by construction, set with update_epic, validated at write time and re-checked at read time. Today's highest-order rule stays as the documented fallback, so undesignated epics behave exactly as before and the existing pin test holds. No structural rule can pick F12 for CQ-F, so the live CQ epics need explicit designations (follow-up task-6a612b08446e4e3cad10bf9cc44cecf6). The honest scope came to about 12 files, so the remaining docs sweep is follow-up task-ec99ee714f174553b91ea0a6b9d2d47a, and this task keeps the files its DoD names (10, at the daemon's limit).
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Two copies of the rule today: delivery/policy.ts isEpicFinalTask (~L202) and an inline block in tools/getContext.ts (~L419-432). getContext already imports delivery/policy transitively through state/dependencyUnblock.
- Consumers: get_context task.isEpicFinal, which the wrappers prefer (scripts/moe-agent.sh ~L8264, .ps1 ~L7355); requiredCheckCommand (strict deliveryPolicy); qa_approve's requiredCheckAtDone snapshot.
- Who writes `order`: a JetBrains drag sends UPDATE_TASK {status, order} (MoeCommandSender.updateTaskStatus); REORDER_TASK goes to taskStore.reorderTask (prev+1 at the end); create_task uses nextTaskOrder, the epic's max + 1. set_task_status itself does not rewrite order.
- update_epic and validateEpicUpdates both whitelist fields (rejectUnknownFields), and the board's UPDATE_EPIC goes through validateEpicUpdates only. loadEntities keeps unknown keys, so the new field round-trips.
- packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/skillFiles.ts is committed and kept in sync with docs/skills by `npm run generate-skill-files`.
planningNotes.risks:
- The live daemon is the IDE-bundled build. Until the plugin is rebuilt and the daemon restarts, a live get_context still gives the old answer for the CQ rows. The DoD-2 evidence is the step-3 fixture test, and the live designations are follow-up task-6a612b08446e4e3cad10bf9cc44cecf6. The SCHEMA, CONFIGURATION and epic-breakdown/qa-loop/regression-check wording is follow-up task-ec99ee714f174553b91ea0a6b9d2d47a.
- A designated final task that is DONE keeps later rows mid-epic until someone re-designates. That is documented behaviour, not a bug.
- Under a strict deliveryPolicy, changing the designation can change which task owes required-check:<qualityGate>. DONE tasks keep their requiredCheckAtDone snapshot; a DONE task without the field is judged live, as with reorders today.
- Do not regenerate skills with npm run build (it rewrites initFiles.ts too). Never edit .moe/, and never git stash in the shared checkout.
- Tests must not read the real board: the CQ fixture is a frozen snapshot copied into the test.
